hook: *3,000 Indians* stuck in Saudi as airports get hit. 40 fly back to Hyderabad tomorrow
tldr: Houthi drone and missile strikes on Saudi infrastructure, including airports, have disrupted flights. About 3,000 Indians are stranded, including 400–500 Umrah pilgrims from Andhra Pradesh; 40 fly back to Hyderabad on Oct 26.

beats.what: Riyadh's airport is closed and Jeddah, Madinah and Dammam face disruptions. Air India, Air India Express and IndiGo suspended Saudi flights until Oct 24; Akasa until Oct 27.
beats.why: Yemen-based Houthi rebels have struck civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including airports, amid the wider Iran–US tensions.
beats.care: Family on Umrah or working in Saudi? Save the Indian control-room numbers below. Check flights on Saudia, Flynas and Flyadeal, which are still running some routes.

cards.body: Jeddah control room: +966-12-2614093 / +966-556122301, toll-free 800-244-0003 (in Saudi), WhatsApp +966-536209704. Riyadh: +966-11-4884697, toll-free 800-2471234, WhatsApp +966-536216082. A new desk is open at the Indian Haj Pilgrims Office in Makkah: +966 553646966.

cards.title: how do people get home?
cards.body: Saudia flies to India from Jeddah, Madinah and Dammam; Flynas from Dammam to Delhi, Mumbai and Lucknow; Flyadeal from Dammam to Mumbai. Connections via the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait or Qatar may work, depending on visa rules.

cards.q: Does anyone in your family travel to the Gulf often?
Which Saudi airport is fully closed?
cards.why: Riyadh's King Khalid airport is closed; the others are operating with disruptions.

viz.l: of them are Umrah pilgrims from Andhra (400–500)

steps.e: Air India, AI Express, IndiGo paused

learn.t: Indian missions abroad run control rooms during crises; registering with them helps them track and evacuate citizens.

watch: Whether Indian airlines resume Saudi flights after Oct 24–27, and more return flights to Hyderabad.
